title: Do Majority-of-Minority Shareholder Voting Rights Reduce Expropriation? Evidence from Related Party Transactions

software.name: SAS
software.description: The four supplied entry programs require SAS. They actively use PROC IMPORT/EXPORT, SORT, SQL, MEANS, RANK, TRANSPOSE, UNIVARIATE, and CORR; imports use XLSX, DLM, and CSV. The saved environment probe records sas_u8 but startup fails at TKELS initialization with return code 1, so version/runtime usability and exact .dta export support are unverified. No additional licensed module is inferred from these procedures.

issues.description: The supplied programs read numerous ISS/Prowess text, CSV, XLSX, and SAS datasets that are absent from this package. The included co_code identifier list is not the analysis data. Exact per-file field, population, fiscal-year history, and compatible acquisition or prepared-input routes remain unresolved.

The source establishes a workable producer order, while the package lacks a driver and configured roots: raw RPT creates WORK.rptfylist, WORK.rptfy1, WORK.snw1, and tn1.rptfy0901; the revision program creates tn1.r1_add_0919 under its separate path2 root; main Part 1 consumes WORK.rptfy1 and Part 2 reads both persistent tn1 members without defining tn1 in that script. Configure the project-relative roots, run the raw-RPT and revision programs before the main program in one SAS session, retain the WORK products, and stage the two persistent members under the main consumer's configured tn1 root. The daily panel is a companion branch that can run after the firm-year RPT output is staged. This is supported preparation; unresolved field contracts are recorded separately.

The main program builds a DATA step named sfin3, then later reads sfin3_5, but the supplied program contains no producer for sfin3_5. Resolve the intended producer and the proper order/schema before treating the main analysis output as constructible.

Main Part 2 consumes item_disc, rabove, and rbelow from tn1.rptfy0901. The supplied raw-RPT producer's firm-year output contains neither these fields nor a source-generation block for them; the inputs may be a separate revision extension, but no compatible producer/file/schema is supplied. Confirm the intended producer, path, keys, and field definitions before using this merge.

Main Part 2 imports capdiv0511.txt from a machine-specific D: drive path, unlike the program's configured relative path root. Stage the exact compatible input under the chosen relative root and change only this path in a working copy.

Main Part 1 joins WORK.rptfy1, whose supplied raw-RPT producer has an explicit KEEP list of unsummed component fields. The next main DATA step names 36 fields including rtotal_sum, rtotal2_sum, and category *_sum variables and fills missing array members with zero. The separate raw-RPT firm-year output is built from rptfy2. The supplied sources do not establish whether the main join is intended to receive these sums or whether zero filling is intentional; do not substitute rptfy2 or manufacture sums without author specification.

The raw-RPT listing block checks bse_delist_date but derives bse_end by inputting nse_delist_date. Because the supplied listing exclusion later uses nse_end or bse_end to select firms, the intended date-to-variable mapping is unresolved; confirm it before interpreting the listing classification. No repair is inferred.

evidence.quote:
The Institutional Shareholder Services (ISS) Global Voting Analytics dataset was
   purchased from ISS by the Columbia University and was received on May 25, 2017.
   The data used to construct RPT variables, accounting variables, stock return variables and
   corporate governance variables were obtained from Prowess, a commercial data vendor.
   The raw data were downloaded on April 15, 2017 from Prowess’s website. To complete
   additional analyses in the revision process, more variables were downloaded from
   Prowess on September 18, 2019.

evidence.description: Datasheet maps three programs to the RPT firm-year data, Section 4/5 samples, and the Section 5.4 daily-return sample, and describes the included identifier list.
evidence.quote:
Computer programs to convert the raw data into the dataset used in the analysis are
   provided with the paper.
   “raw rpt to firm-year rpt” converts raw RPT data (at the firm-year-party level) to a firm-
   year level RPT dataset.
   “merge data and construct sample” converts the processed firm-year level RPT data and
   the raw data of financial statement, stock return, corporate governance, and shareholder
   voting to the voting outcome sample used in Section 4 and the real effect sample used in
   Section 5.
   “construct daily return panel” converts raw daily stock return data to the daily return sample
   used in Section 5.4.
   A list of firm identifier for the sample used in the main analysis is also provided. The firm
   identifier is Prowess’s company code (“co_code”).

review_notes: The assessed full_pipeline includes all four supplied SAS programs. No analysis_only scope is supported because the package contains no compatible author-prepared analysis dataset or complete analysis-only route; the packaged identifier CSV is not analysis data.

All 35 frozen read dependencies are reviewed: 31 point to 24 mandatory data requirements, three are generated outputs with supplied producers, and one targets the unresolved item_disc/rabove/rbelow field contract. No read was labeled optional. Every selected data requirement, software dependency, and issue has a linked action.

The supported order is raw RPT conversion, revision-variable preparation, then the main sample program in one SAS session for the WORK handoffs; configure relative roots and stage tn1.rptfy0901 and tn1.r1_add_0919 for the main consumer. The daily-return panel is a companion branch after its firm-year RPT output is staged. The RPTFY1 36-field contract, item_disc/rabove/rbelow, sfin3_5, and id_0719 BSE-date mapping remain specifically unresolved.

A bounded read confirms the local RISK.GLOBALVOTERESULTS candidate is readable and has voting fields, but it exposes MGMTrec (Management Recommendation), not the source's ISSrec; product equivalence and 2014–2015 coverage are unverified, so it is not substituted.

The available SAS environment probe records a TKELS startup failure with return code 1. SAS runtime/version and import/export component availability are unverified; this is not treated as a license barrier.

No author program, estimator, or analysis dataset was executed. The work used static source review, frozen catalog lookup results, and one bounded row_limit=1 read; all command, helper, and probe outcomes are preserved under the assigned generation_001/probes directory.
